login.title: Sign in
login.text: Enter the dashboard token: Bridge__Web__Token in your .env, or – if you didn't set one – the token the bridge made, shown with: docker compose exec tesla-bridge cat /data/web-token
log.title: Recent commands
log.sub: From this dashboard, Home Assistant or anything else that talks to the bridge.
controls.lede: Everything here is also available as entities in Home Assistant. Purple means the bridge is waiting for the car to confirm.
c.seatsHint: Tap a seat to change the heat
data.lede: Every value the bridge knows, where it came from, and the raw stream from the car.
data.rawhint: Exactly what the car sent before the bridge translated it.
data.cfgHint: The car sends to {0}. The status should say "synced": true.
data.waiting: Waiting for data from the car…
confirm.push: Send the telemetry configuration to the car now?
usage.lede: What the bridge has used of Tesla's Fleet API this month, priced at Tesla's rates. The first $10 each month are free.
usage.proj: expected by the end of the month
usage.hintNone: The projection appears after the first day of the month.
usage.hintOver: At this rate you will go over the free credit. Make the busiest fields less frequent under Settings.
usage.hintOk: At this rate you will use {0} % of the free credit.
usage.note: Only counts what goes through the bridge. Other apps using your Tesla account are not included; the final number is under Usage on developer.tesla.com.
settings.lede: Choose which values the car sends and how often. The car only sends a value when it changes, so fields that rarely change cost nothing even at 1 second. Driving and charging values are the ones that add up.
settings.presetsSub: Sets every field that changes all the time while driving or charging. Other fields stay at 1 second.
preset.economySub: Updates every 30 s to a few minutes while driving
preset.defaultSub: The bridge's defaults, around $2–5 a month
preset.liveSub: Location and speed every second – costs more
settings.fieldsSub: Off means the car stops sending the value, and the matching entity in Home Assistant stops updating.
settings.snapshotSub: Fills in values the car hasn't streamed yet (one data request, $0.002). Never wakes the car.
settings.estNone: The estimate appears once the car has streamed for a while.
settings.saved: Saved and sent to the car. It picks up the change the next time it is online.
settings.pushFail: Saved, but it couldn't be sent to the car: {0}. The bridge tries again within 12 hours.
confirm.reset: Reset every field to the bridge's defaults and send them to the car?
unsaved: You have unsaved changes on the settings page.
setup.lede: The steps to connect the bridge to your car. Everything here is a one-time job.
s.keyMissing: No key in {0}. Restart the bridge and it will be created.
s.appMissing: Set Bridge__Tesla__ClientId, Bridge__Tesla__ClientSecret and Bridge__Telemetry__Hostname in .env and restart.
s.regUnknown: Not checked yet. The bridge registers by itself as soon as the public key is reachable from the internet.
s.regOk: Tesla has the same key as the bridge.
s.regOther: Tesla has a DIFFERENT key registered for the domain. Press Register to update it.
s.regNo: Not registered yet. The bridge keeps trying by itself – is the public key reachable from the internet?
s.loginOk: The bridge has access to your car.
s.loginNo: Opens Tesla's sign-in page, then a page that confirms the sign-in.
s.pairOk: The car has the app's key.
s.pairNo: Scan with the phone that has the Tesla app, or open the link. Then tap your key card in the car.
s.teleWait: The configuration was sent, but the car hasn't picked it up. Wake the car in the Tesla app and wait a few minutes.
s.teleNone: Sent automatically after sign-in. Press Check status to see whether the car has it.
car3d.allClosed: Everything is closed. Drag to turn the car; tap a dot to open.
frunkManual: The frunk is closed by hand.
model.title: Car view
ver.how: Update on the server: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
seatClimate.title: Seat and steering-wheel heat
seatClimate.sub: The car only heats seats and the steering wheel while the climate is on. What should happen when you turn them on with the climate off?
seatClimate.on: Turn the climate on as well (like the Tesla app)
seatClimate.off: Nothing – show that the climate must be on first
c.seatsNeedClimate: Turns the climate on as well – the car only heats seats while it is on
c.seatsClimateOff: The climate must be on – the car only heats seats while it is on
ble.title: Bluetooth (ESP32)
ble.sub: Optional. An ESP32 near where the car parks sends commands and wake-ups over Bluetooth while the car is in range – free and without the internet. Away from home the Fleet API is used as before.
ble.offSub: No ESP32 – everything goes through the Fleet API.
ble.inRange: Car in range – commands go over Bluetooth
ble.away: ESP32 connected – the car isn't nearby
ble.notTesla: The ESP32 answers, but doesn't have the Tesla BLE entities. Flash esphome/tesla-ble.yaml from the repository.
ble.pairTitle: Pair the ESP32 with the car (once)
ble.pair1: Sit in the car with your key card.
ble.pair3: Tap the key card on the console between the front seats and confirm on the car's screen.
ble.pairSent: Now tap your key card in the car and confirm on the screen.
ble.howTitle: How do I get an ESP32 running?
ble.how: Any ESP32 dev board (about 50 kr.) works. Flash esphome/tesla-ble.yaml from the repository with ESPHome, then type its address here. Your car shows up in Bluetooth scanner apps as {0} – that's how you find its MAC address. Step-by-step guide
credit: 3D model: “{1}” by {2}, {4}, modified
model.none: No model yet – the Car page shows the drawing.
model.how1: Any glTF binary (.glb) shows, up to 80 MB. Convert .obj, .fbx or .gltf to .glb in Blender (File → Export → glTF 2.0, format glTF Binary). Instead of uploading, you can also put the file in ./config/bridge/car.glb on the server.
model.how2: For doors that open, spinning wheels and the colour picker, name the parts door_fl, door_fr, door_rl, door_rr and wheel_fl … wheel_rr, and the materials paint (body) and seats (interior). The front should face +Z and the driver's side +X.
loc.noAddress: No address found for this spot
loc.mapOff: Map and address are turned off under Settings
map.title: Map and address
map.sub: The Car page shows where the car is on a map, with its street address. The bridge looks the address up at OpenStreetMap (Nominatim), and your browser loads the map from OpenStreetMap, so OpenStreetMap sees the car's position. Off: only the coordinates are shown, and the position stays in your network.
map.on: Show the map and the address
mqttOpen.title: Your MQTT broker lets anyone in
mqttOpen.text: It accepts logins without a password, and the bridge takes commands over MQTT – so any device on your network can send tesla/<VIN>/cmd/unlock. Require logins in the broker (Mosquitto: allow_anonymous false and a password_file), or set Bridge__Mqtt__Commands=false in .env if you only use the Home Assistant integration. See docs/security.md.
